full_details: In the morning the tables named the boy, a girl who reads, ribbons, gloves, and a horse, and did not name a child. At Holywell Richard Burbage gave up the old lath sword and said it had killed four Richmonds. At Paul's you bought a riddle-book for a girl who reads, and in Bishopsgate Street ribbons in three colours and a pair of perfumed gloves. Last, at the Bull, the ostler showed the bay's teeth, and you pretended to judge them. The horse is sound, a little sour, and bespoken from Wednesday the twenty-sixth at twelvepence a day and his own fodder. Nothing was paid down. At home the book took six lines: the sword at no price, the riddle-book at twopence, the ribbons at fivepence, the gloves at two shillings and fourpence, the bay not yet had, and a sum of two shillings and elevenpence. Saturday's part was not entered again. No coffer total was written. The letter is still unsent.
one_sentence: You took Burbage's old lath sword at Holywell, bought for the children at Paul's and in Bishopsgate Street, bespoke a sour bay from Wednesday week at twelvepence a day, and wrote six lines in the book.
title: A sour bay bespoken, and six lines
